tasks.short: Advise owners during the consultation on care, feeding and treatment options, draft replies to follow-up questions, send them, prepare written care instructions, and note the advice in the record.

steps.what: Veterinarian advises animal owners on medical conditions and treatment options during the consultation
Veterinarian writes replies to owners' follow-up questions about feeding and general care

loop.input: The owner's question, the animal's record and the practice's vetted care texts.
loop.output: A draft reply quoting the care texts.
loop.check: Every advice sentence must cite a paragraph from the vetted care texts or it is dropped; the veterinarian reads each cited paragraph to see that it supports the sentence and fits this animal; questions about new symptoms are not drafted and unclear cases are written by hand.
loop.stop: One draft per question; questions about new symptoms are not drafted and go to the veterinarian.
loop.why_not_simpler: Owners ask in their own words; a fixed FAQ does not match their animal's case.

steps.what: Veterinarian checks the final reply: the advice fits this animal and the question, and it goes to the right owner
Veterinarian sends the checked reply to the owner
Veterinarian prepares written care instructions on sanitary measures and treatment
Veterinarian notes the advice given in the record

tasks.design: Standard care sheets per condition sit in the practice system ({OTHER}) and are adapted per animal, so written instructions are not typed each time. For follow-up questions by e-mail, a bounded step drafts a reply from the practice's vetted care texts; every advice sentence must cite a care text, questions about new symptoms are not drafted, and the veterinarian checks every reply and sends it. Advising owners in the consultation stays with the veterinarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Instructions and replies were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems hold care sheets; language models draft replies from vetted texts.
tasks.human_edge: Helping an owner decide when to stop treatment.
tasks.altitude: The veterinarian approves drafted replies instead of writing each one.

reach.learn: Whether care texts cover common questions.

evidence.claim: Thuisarts publishes guideline-based patient information, the model for drafting only from vetted texts.
Once a tool proposes diagnoses or treatment it can become a regulated device; here drafts only quote care texts.

assumptions: Boundary: from the consultation to advice noted; treatment is outside.
Input contract: care texts written and kept by the practice; fallback is writing replies by hand.

The veterinarian checks every reply (s2b) and sends it (s3 keeps 10). s2 keeps 60 for reading drafts and their care texts; s4 keeps 40 for adapting care sheets. s5 is a first record of the advice and keeps its full time.
Owners read replies as before; no added owner time.
research_questions: How many drafted replies does the veterinarian change?

already_counted.description: Veterinarian reads and edits drafted replies.

incremental.description: Veterinarian keeps the care texts current.

approvals.approved_version: The reply exactly as checked by the veterinarian in s2b, sent once by e-mail to this owner; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: care texts cover few of the questions, so s2 keeps 80, and care sheets need much adapting, so s4 keeps 70 (12.3); high: texts and sheets cover most cases (20.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Choose courses and conferences, register for them, attend lectures and continuing education, and log continuing education points.

steps.what: Veterinarian chooses continuing education courses
Veterinarian checks the registration before sending: course, date, fee and own details
Veterinarian registers for the course
Veterinarian attends lectures, conferences or continuing education courses
Course providers register the veterinarian's attendance points in the professional registry
Veterinarian logs continuing education points: from certificates by hand today; after the change checks that providers registered them and logs the rest

tasks.design: The professional registry's course list shows accredited courses with points by subject, and course providers register attendance points directly in the registry, so the veterinarian does not log certificates by hand. Choosing, registering and attending stay with the veterinarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Courses were found in mailings and points logged from certificates.
tasks.enabler_now: Professional registries list accredited courses and take points from providers.
tasks.still_hard: Practice cover is needed for every day away.
tasks.human_edge: Bringing back a technique the whole practice can use.

evidence.claim: Professional registries can list accredited courses and take attendance points from providers.

assumptions: Boundary: from education needs to points logged; course content is outside.
Input contract: providers register points; fallback is logging certificates.
Course fees are approved as today.
Providers' registration (s3b, share 1) is outside the veterinarian's savings. s4 keeps 30 for checking the registry and logging points providers did not register.
research_questions: Is the registry complete at re-registration?

incremental.description: No new work: checking that points arrived is inside s4.

approvals.approved_version: The registration for the chosen course with date, fee and own details exactly as checked by the veterinarian in s1b, sent once to the course provider; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many providers do not register points, so s4 keeps 70 (6.3); high: most providers register as designed (10.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Show and supervise assistants handling animals, write work instructions and protocols, plan assistants' duties, and record training done.

steps.what: Veterinarian trains and supervises workers who handle or care for animals
Veterinarian writes work instructions and protocols
Veterinarian checks the final protocol: steps are right for this practice's animals, drugs and equipment, and it goes to the right staff
Veterinarian publishes the checked protocol to the assistants
Veterinarian plans assistants' duties in a spreadsheet
Veterinarian checks the duty plan: every session and surgery is covered by an assistant with the right skills, and no one is planned when absent
Veterinarian publishes the checked duty plan in the agenda
Veterinarian records training done: on paper today, ticked on a skills checklist per assistant after the change

tasks.design: Work instructions sit in a shared protocol library ({DOCS}) that the practice adapts instead of each veterinarian writing their own. Assistants' duties are planned in the practice system's agenda ({CALENDAR}) together with appointments. Training done is ticked off on a skills checklist per assistant; this first record keeps its time. The veterinarian checks and publishes each protocol and duty plan. Showing and supervising animal handling stay with the veterinarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Protocols were written by each veterinarian, duties planned in spreadsheets and training on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared protocol libraries and practice agendas are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Animal handling is learned by doing, not reading.
tasks.human_edge: Teaching an assistant to read a frightened dog's body language.

evidence.claim: Shared protocol libraries and practice agendas are standard tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from staff on duty to training recorded; hiring is outside.
Input contract: protocol library kept by the practice; fallback is own protocols and spreadsheets.

s2 keeps 60 for adapting library protocols to the practice. s3 keeps 60: appointments show in the agenda, but the veterinarian still decides duties. The checks and publications (s2b, s2c, s3b, s3c) take 1 each. s4 is a first record and keeps its full time.

incremental.description: No new work: adapting shared protocols is the remaining work of s2.

approvals.approved_version: The protocol text and version exactly as checked by the veterinarian in s2b, published once to the practice's assistants in the protocol library; any change needs a new check.
The assistants' duty plan for the period exactly as checked by the veterinarian in s3b, published once in the practice agenda; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the library fits few procedures, so s2 keeps 85, and duties are still planned beside the agenda, so s3 keeps 80 (3.5); high: library and agenda used as designed (8.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Schedule appointments, accept payments, keep business records, prepare the budget, and decide on it.

steps.what: Veterinarian schedules appointments by phone
Owner books a routine appointment online in the practice system
Veterinarian checks the invoice before payment: lines and amount match the treatment given, and it is for the right owner
Veterinarian takes payment: typed into the terminal at the desk today; after the change the terminal takes the checked invoice amount, or the owner pays by a link
Veterinarian maintains business records: typed in today; after the change checks the imported bank and payment lines and books them in the accounting package
Veterinarian prepares the budget in a spreadsheet
Veterinarian decides on the budget

tasks.design: Owners book routine appointments online in the practice system ({OTHER}), so fewer bookings come by phone. The payment terminal is linked to the invoice, and owners can pay by link. Bank and payment data flow into the accounting package ({ERP}), and a dashboard ({BI}) gives revenue and costs for the budget. Deciding the budget stays with the veterinarian.
tasks.previous_blocker: Bookings came by phone, payments were entered by hand and the budget built from exports.
tasks.enabler_now: Practice systems take online bookings and link payments; bank feeds fill accounting.
tasks.still_hard: Urgent cases cannot be booked online.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding to invest in a new scanner the practice can just afford.
tasks.altitude: The veterinarian decides on figures instead of compiling them.

evidence.claim: Practice systems take online bookings and link payments to invoices; bank feeds fill accounting packages.

assumptions: Boundary: from the owner request to the budget decided; tax filing is outside.
Input contract: practice and bank data connected to accounting; fallback is phone and spreadsheets.
Owners book online (s1b, share 1, customer time) in about the time a call took.
Budget decisions stay with the veterinarian.

s1 keeps 40 for urgent and complex bookings by phone. s2 keeps 60 for the payment itself; typing amounts goes. s3 keeps 40 for checking and booking imported lines; the veterinarian books them, so nothing posts without them. s4 keeps 50 for estimating the coming year.

incremental.description: Veterinarian keeps online booking slots current.

approvals.approved_version: The invoice with lines and amount exactly as checked by the veterinarian in s1c, presented once at the terminal or sent once as a payment link to the owner's address on file; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many urgent cases still come by phone, so s1 keeps 70, and the bank link covers part of the accounts, so s3 keeps 70 (31.1); high: mostly routine bookings online and full bank links (47.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The veterinarian keeps advising owners, learning, supervising staff and deciding the budget; written replies, phone bookings and spreadsheets shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A veterinarian with more time for animals and owners.
